Investment firm FBN started coverage on marketing software firm HubSpot
with a Sector Perform rating and a $230 price target on Wednesday.

"HubSpot is a high-quality software asset — one unified agentic customer platform rather than a suite assembled through M&A — with over 306,000 customers, an owned freemium-and-partner demand engine, and revenue and NG EPS beats in each of the last ten quarters," analyst Shebly Seyrafi wrote in a note to clients. "The September 17 Analyst Day reset what investors are being asked to underwrite. Management guided FY2027 NG operating [margin percentage] to 23–24% from roughly 21% in FY2026, raised the 2030 framework to a 30% NG operating margin, and for the first time attached a 20% GAAP operating margin and stock-based compensation at 10% of revenue to the same date. Absolute SBC falls to an estimated $511M in FY2026 from $528M in FY2025 — the first dollar decline in HubSpot's public history."

However, Seyrafi acknowledged there are some negatives for HubSpot going forward, notably in the near-term. The company added just 6,988 customers on a net basis in the second-quarter, down from the guided of 9,000 to 10,000, due largely to trials and sales retraining, as well as a tougher demand environment.

title: FBN starts coverage on HubSpot with Sector Perform rating
